title: HMOX1 controls a heme-ferritin switch that protects cells from ferroptosis.
takeaway: Reports that when HMOX1 is inactive, heme is stabilized rather than catabolised, and that this stabilized heme up-regulates ferritin and suppresses ferroptosis, rescuing cell death caused by both pharmacological and genetic GPX4 inhibition. The authors frame this as a heme-HMOX1-ferritin axis setting ferroptosis sensitivity.
caveat: The abstract describes cell-level experiments only and names no tumour model or in vivo test; the therapeutic use it raises is proposed, not shown.

title: Metabolic rewiring driven by phosphoglycolate phosphatase deletion inhibits ferroptosis.
takeaway: Deleting phosphoglycolate phosphatase (PGP) suppresses ferroptosis by rewiring the pentose phosphate pathway and cellular energy and lipid metabolism into a multifactorial antioxidant response. Separately, the reported PGP inhibitor CP1 turns out to sensitize cells to ferroptosis and is characterized as a direct dual inhibitor of PGP and FSP1 that also triggers FSP1 self-assembly.
caveat: The abstract names genetic, biochemical and biophysical approaches without saying which experimental system each was done in, and mentions no animal or disease model, so CP1 is presented as a pharmacological tool rather than a validated therapeutic.

title: Ferroptosis induction via genetic approaches - CRISPR/Cas9-based disruption on key anti-ferroptotic genes.
takeaway: A methods chapter, not new findings: it sets out a CRISPR/Cas9 protocol for making SLC7A11- and GPX4-knockout HT1080 cells as a genetic alternative to erastin and (1S,3R)-RSL3, whose off-target effects the authors note (erastin on mitochondrial voltage-dependent anion channels, RSL3 on other selenoproteins). The knockout lines need beta-mercaptoethanol or liproxstatin-1 in the medium, and withdrawing the supplement induces ferroptosis.
caveat: This is a protocol chapter rather than a report of new results: the abstract describes a procedure in one cell line (HT1080), so it is a method to use, not evidence about ferroptosis biology.

title: Double-bond geometry determines fatty acid metabolic fate and ferroptosis sensitivity.
takeaway: A screen of structurally diverse fatty acids identifies trans-unsaturated fatty acids as ferroptosis sensitizers: the trans PUFA linoelaidic acid enhanced lipid peroxidation more than its cis counterpart linoleic acid, and the trans monounsaturated petroselaidic acid also sensitized cells while its cis isomer petroselinic acid suppressed ferroptosis. Petroselaidic acid required stearoyl-CoA desaturase-dependent conversion to a PUFA, which the authors read as double-bond geometry redirecting a fatty acid metabolic fate.
caveat: A preprint, so not yet peer reviewed, and the abstract reports cell-level lipidomic and sensitivity experiments with no animal or dietary model, leaving any physiological consequence of trans-fat geometry untested.

title: 15-LOX-catalytic bias towards ether-(alkenyl)-ETE-PEs oxidation bestows selectivity of PRO-ferroptotic cell death signaling.
takeaway: Using redox lipidomics with biochemical, biophysical, genetic and molecular dynamics approaches, the authors find both 15-LOX isoforms selectively oxidize alkyl/alkenyl-ETE-PE, but not the PC equivalents, to 15-HpETE-PEs and trigger ferroptosis independently of the sn-1 vinyl bond. They measure sn-1 vinyl bond peroxidation as roughly 500-fold slower than sn-2-ETE-PE, which they take to exclude an antioxidant role for plasmalogens in ferroptosis, and report the sn-1-alkenyl-sn-2-15-HpETE-PE product as a pathogenic factor in asthma, cancer, brain trauma and skin UVB injury.
caveat: The abstract asserts the oxidized lipid acts as a pathogenic factor in those four settings without describing the experiments behind it, so what was measured, tested or blocked in each is left unspecified, and the therapeutic target it proposes is untested.

title: Targeted extracellular degradation of LRP8 promotes ferroptosis in cancer cells.
takeaway: Targeted extracellular degradation of the selenium uptake receptor LRP8, using bispecific KineTAC chimeras that route it to the lysosome through cytokine receptor internalisation, lowers several selenoproteins including GPX4 and sensitizes cancer cells to ferroptosis. The authors present receptor-mediated selenium uptake as a targetable node in ferroptosis resistance.
caveat: A preprint, so not yet peer reviewed, and the abstract reports sensitization in cancer cells with no in vivo efficacy, selectivity or toxicity data, so overcoming therapy resistance is framed as a broader prospect rather than a result.

title: Polyamines buffer labile iron to suppress ferroptosis.
takeaway: Polyamines are shown to buffer redox-active iron: a genome-wide CRISPR screen found polyamine depletion synthetically lethal with loss of GPX4, and polyamine deficiency redistributed cellular iron, enlarging the labile iron pool and up-regulating ferritin. A new genetically encoded fluorescent reporter for redox-active iron showed an inverse correlation between polyamine levels and redox-active iron in single living cells.
caveat: The abstract reports cultured-cell screening and live-cell imaging only; the implications it draws for ferroptosis-linked disease states are stated as implications, with no animal or patient data behind them.

title: Suppression of Lipid Peroxidation by Necrostatins and Their Potential for Dual Targeting of Ferroptosis and Necroptosis.
takeaway: Explains how the RIPK1 inhibitor necrostatin-1 also blocks ferroptosis: its thiohydantoin reacts with hydroperoxides to give a sulfenic acid that traps peroxyl radicals and inhibits lipid peroxidation. Analogs tested in the cell-free FENIX assay gained anti-peroxidation activity with more steric bulk or nucleophilicity near the thiocarbonyl, with the methyl group relocated, or with a fully conjugated linker; the fully conjugated dsNec-1, isolated as a stable species, is suggested to mediate the anti-ferroptotic effect, but desaturated derivatives were inactive against necroptosis, so the authors conclude the scaffold is unsuitable for dual-pathway inhibitors.
caveat: The structure-activity work rests on the cell-free FENIX lipid peroxidation assay, and the abstract reports no cellular ferroptosis protection for the new analogs, so dsNec-1 mediating Nec-1 activity in cells is suggested rather than shown.

title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression.
takeaway: Reports KY0418, an orally dosed, plasma-stable covalent GPX4 inhibitor with an isourea warhead that targets GPX4 at SeCys46 and induces ferroptosis hallmarks in human and mouse cancer cell lines with greater selectivity than existing inhibitors. In mice it reproduces ferroptotic changes in an acute-liver-injury model, remodels tissue metabolism and generates detectable hydroxyl radicals, and across cancer models consistently eradicated circulating tumor cells and suppressed metastasis.
caveat: Shown in cancer cell lines and in mice; the abstract reports subcutaneous-tumor responses ranged from no effect to about 70% growth inhibition, and positions KY0418 as a tool for in vivo research and translation rather than a treatment tested in patients.

title: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression.
takeaway: Describes designed mitochondria-targeting tetraoxane compounds (WMK-1/2) that initiate local lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis without first inhibiting GPX4 or FSP1. The abstract reports WMK-1 localizes to mitochondria, impairs oxidative phosphorylation, and drives a labile-Fe2+-dependent "mito-ferroptosis" that is rescued by lipophilic radical-trapping antioxidants and by alpha-lipoic acid but is insensitive to ACSL4 perturbation and PUFA supplementation; WMK-1/2 are bioavailable, suppress tumors, and augment immune-checkpoint blockers.
caveat: The GPX4/FSP1-independent sub-pathway rests on the rescue and perturbation experiments the abstract lists, and efficacy is reported in cell and mouse cancer models, not in patients.

title: Pooled Screening of Cancer Cell Lines Identifies Vulnerability to Polyunsaturated Fatty-Acid-Induced Ferroptosis.
takeaway: A barcoded, pooled screen across 554 cancer cell lines from 19 lineages finds a subset sensitive to polyunsaturated fatty acids at physiological concentrations, with PUFA treatment alone sufficient to induce ferroptosis in lines that are also vulnerable to GPX4 inhibition. PUFA sensitivity is positively associated with FABP1 expression, conjugated linolenic acids also induce ferroptosis, and a genome-wide CRISPR screen in ES2 cells defines a pro-ferroptosis route converting PUFAs to membrane phospholipids and an anti-ferroptosis route diverting them to lipid droplets.
caveat: The dataset is cultured cell lines; the FABP1 link is reported as a positive association across lines rather than a tested mechanism, and the abstract suggests the dietary-metabolite therapeutic avenue rather than showing it in animals.

title: Mammals produce cyclo-octasulfur to suppress lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis.
takeaway: Reports that mammals harbor elemental sulfur as cyclo-octasulfur (S8), accumulating to millimolar concentrations in mitochondrial membranes and lipid droplets of mouse and human cells, and identifies lipid-droplet-associated nitric oxide synthase as a source of its biosynthesis. S8 in lipid droplets limits lipid peroxidation and suppresses ferroptosis, and intra-articular injection of solubilized S8 reduced lipid peroxidation in a mouse osteoarthritis model.
caveat: Based on mouse and human cells plus one osteoarthritis mouse model where injected S8 lowered lipid peroxidation, a redox readout rather than a disease outcome; the abstract states the protective role as one S8 "may" play.

title: Targeted extracellular degradation of LRP8 promotes ferroptosis in cancer cells.
takeaway: Identifies targeted extracellular degradation of the selenium-uptake receptor LRP8 as a way to lower the ferroptosis-protective enzyme GPX4: bispecific KineTAC chimeras couple LRP8 to cytokine-receptor internalization and route it to the lysosome, reducing several selenoproteins including GPX4 and sensitizing cancer cells to ferroptosis. The authors frame receptor-mediated selenium uptake as a targetable node in ferroptosis resistance.
caveat: The results the abstract describes are at the cell level (reduced selenoprotein abundance and sensitization of cancer cells); overcoming therapy resistance is presented as a framework the approach could enable, not a demonstrated outcome.

title: On the Inhibition of Lipid Peroxidation and Ferroptosis by Fatty Acids.
takeaway: Tests whether replacing oxidizable PUFAs with non-oxidizable fatty acids is a general way to suppress ferroptosis by preparing cyclopropanated PUFAs (CP-PUFAs), predicted to be far less reactive to peroxyl radicals while keeping cis geometry. CP-PUFAs suppressed erastin2- and RSL3-induced ferroptosis in HT-1080 and HEK-293 cells much as deuterated PUFAs and MUFAs did while palmitate did not, with CP2-LA comparable to D-PUFAs but CP4-AA only modest, and lipidomics showed accompanying lipid remodeling.
caveat: Tested in two cultured cell lines against two chemical inducers; the authors state the strategy is general only provided the non-oxidizable fatty acid can be used by biosynthetic machinery and is not lipotoxic at the concentrations needed for protection.

title: PLA2G2F suppresses ferroptosis through phospholipid remodeling.
takeaway: Identifies the secretory phospholipase PLA2G2F as a ferroptosis suppressor in bladder cancer that acts intracellularly from the endoplasmic reticulum. The abstract reports that PPARG upregulates PLA2G2F and that PPARG-mediated ferroptosis resistance largely depends on it, that lipidomic profiling indicates PLA2G2F preferentially acts on ether-linked PUFA phospholipids to shrink the peroxidation-prone pool, and that inhibiting PPARG signaling or PLA2G2F sensitizes bladder cancer cells to ferroptosis.
caveat: Shown in bladder cancer; the preferential action on ether-linked PUFA phospholipids is what the abstract says the lipidomic profiling "suggests," and the sensitization is reported in bladder cancer cells.

title: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer.
takeaway: In small cell lung cancer, integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis finds a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine across neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine states. On cysteine depletion, ASCL1-low cells undergo ferroptosis while ASCL1-high cells undergo apoptosis and resist ferroptosis, a resistance the abstract attributes to ASCL1 directly activating GCH1 and raising BH4/BH2 antioxidants; combining cysteine depletion with inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts.
caveat: Demonstrated in small cell lung cancer models, including defined cell states and patient-derived xenografts; the cell-death switch and the ASCL1-GCH1-BH4 mechanism are shown for SCLC and not claimed beyond it.

title: Cryo-EM structures reveal the mechanism of phosphatidylserine remodeling by membrane-bound glycerophospholipid O-acyltransferase 1.
takeaway: Reports that MBOAT1 preferentially makes monounsaturated-fatty-acid-containing phosphatidylserine from lyso-PS, and presents high-resolution cryo-EM structures of human MBOAT1 capturing distinct binding poses of the fatty-acyl donor, the lyso-PS acceptor and the PS product. With lipidomics, enzymology and molecular dynamics the authors lay out the mechanism and pathway of MBOAT1-dependent PS remodeling.
caveat: A preprint, so not yet peer reviewed, and what the abstract reports is structural, enzymatic, lipidomic and simulation work: the connection to ferroptosis appears as background for why PS acyl-chain remodeling matters, not as a ferroptosis measurement of its own.

title: The rise of reducing reagent-resistant TfR1 dimer marks ferroptosis.
takeaway: Identifies a reducing-reagent-resistant (3R) dimer of transferrin receptor 1 as a highly specific indicator of lipid peroxidation: it rises when ferroptosis is induced either pharmacologically or by genetic perturbation, and it can be detected in tissue and in extracellular vesicles isolated from mouse or patient plasma, which the authors offer as a way to detect disease-associated ferroptosis.
caveat: The broader utility is what the authors "posit" from TfR1 being near-ubiquitously expressed; what the abstract reports is detection of the 3R dimer in cells, in tissue and in extracellular vesicles from mouse and patient plasma.

title: Proteasome inhibition bidirectionally regulates ferroptosis sensitivity.
takeaway: Separates proteasome inhibition from the apoptosis it normally causes, using small-molecule inducers, pathway-specific death inhibitors and direct death imaging, and finds it cuts both ways: proteasome inhibition sensitizes cells to ferroptosis from GPX4 inhibition while making them resistant to ferroptosis from system xc- inhibition. The sensitization needs protein synthesis but not the apoptosis execution machinery, and the ATF4 stress response opposes it.
caveat: Each direction is tied to a particular inducer class in cell experiments, so the context-dependence the abstract claims is defined by which ferroptosis inducer was used rather than by tissue or in vivo setting.

title: Enhancing the efficacy of B7-H3-targeting antibody-drug conjugate DS-7300a in TP53-deficient tumors by inducing ferroptosis.
takeaway: Using prostate cancer as a model, reports that the B7-H3-targeting antibody-drug conjugate DS-7300a depends on functional p53, with TP53 defects conferring resistance: its DXd payload causes DNA damage that activates ATM/ATR/CHK and stabilizes p53, while TP53-deficient cells fail to sense the damage. In those resistant cells DS-7300a raises lipid peroxidation and upregulates GPX4, and inhibiting GPX4 to induce ferroptosis improved DS-7300a efficacy in isogenic xenografts and a newly developed humanized B7-H3 model.
caveat: Shown with prostate cancer as the model system and in mouse xenograft models; the abstract presents ferroptosis induction as a promising approach to overcome resistance rather than a combination tested in patients.

title: Autophagic degradation of RAB8A promotes ferroptosis through dysregulation of TFRC-mediated iron uptake.
takeaway: Identifies RAB8A as a selective autophagy substrate that normally restrains ferroptosis. Ferroptotic stress triggers RNF126-dependent polyubiquitination and SQSTM1-mediated, ATG5/ATG7-dependent degradation of RAB8A; losing RAB8A sensitizes cancer cells while a degradation-resistant mutant suppresses death. RAB8A binds TFRC and helps move it from the plasma membrane to endolysosomes, so its loss impairs TFRC clearance and raises iron uptake, Fe2+ and lipid peroxidation. RAB8A depletion improved ferroptosis-inducing therapy in fibrosarcoma and pancreatic cancer xenografts.
caveat: The in vivo work is xenograft models, and the clinical part of the abstract is an association between RAB8A level, poor prognosis and ferroptosis resistance in pancreatic cancer rather than an intervention tested in patients.

title: LZTFL1 rewires NADPH-glutathione metabolism to amplify ferroptosis.
takeaway: Identifies LZTFL1 as a ferroptosis regulator that rewires glutathione metabolism: it promotes oxidation of G6PD, limiting NADPH production and GSH regeneration, and the resulting GSH depletion in turn boosts LZTFL1 translation through AKT-mTOR-eIF4E, a feedforward loop that amplifies ferroptosis. In vivo the LZTFL1-FHOD1-G6PD axis sensitized several tumor models including patient-derived xenografts, with more lipid peroxidation, less GSH, slower tumor growth and longer survival, and LZTFL1 restored cisplatin sensitivity in resistant lung and ovarian cancer cells.
caveat: The patient-level claim is that LZTFL1 expression predicts improved survival in lung adenocarcinoma, a correlation, and the re-sensitization by FDA-approved agents is reported in resistant tumor models; the abstract frames LZTFL1 as a potential biomarker and target.

title: Perforin triggers iron-induced mitochondrial damage to drive ferroptosis and anti-tumor immunity.
takeaway: Describes a granzyme-independent job for perforin: Prf1 itself drives tumor-cell ferroptosis. Its pore formation triggers endocytosis of the transferrin receptor and so raises iron uptake, and it promotes endosomal-mitochondrial contacts that load mitochondria with iron, causing mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis. Dietary iron supplementation slowed tumor progression in murine models in a Prf1-dependent way.
caveat: The mechanism and the dietary-iron result come from murine tumor models, and the patient-level statement is a correlation between Prf1 expression, survival and response to checkpoint blockade rather than an intervention that was tested.

title: Leishmania infantum triggers lipid peroxidation and non-canonical cell death in macrophages.
takeaway: A negative result for ferroptosis: in LPS-primed mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages, Leishmania infantum causes a delayed death that does not need GSDMD or the inflammasome, and that survives combined deletion of caspase-8, RIPK3 and caspase-1/11. The death came with robust lipid peroxidation, yet ferrostatin-1 did not rescue viability and deleting GPX4 raised lipid peroxidation without making infected macrophages die more, which the authors read as the parasite uncoupling lipid peroxidation from cell death.
caveat: In mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages, and the abstract's own conclusion is that this is lipid peroxidation without ferroptosis: the death pathway is named only as non-canonical and independent of the pathways they tested, so what it is remains open.

title: Development of isourea-based covalent GPX4 inhibitors and structure-activity relationship analysis in ferroptosis induction.
takeaway: A medicinal-chemistry campaign building covalent GPX4 inhibitors around a heterobenzylic isourea used as a tunable leaving group, inspired by the SN2-like geometry of GPX4 catalysis. Systematic variation of substituent, scaffold, rigidity, side chain and stereochemistry gave structure-activity relationships; an intermediate confirmed on-target ferroptotic activity through lipid peroxidation and liproxstatin-1-rescuable cytotoxicity, and optimization produced two orally bioavailable leads — compound 418 as a potent cellular probe (IC50 7.7 nM) and compound 380, whose oral dosing suppressed tumour growth in 786-O and MDA-MB-468 xenografts.
caveat: Potency is cell-line IC50s and efficacy is two mouse xenograft models; the membrane-related binding evidence is NMR measured under a detergent membrane-mimetic (DPC) rather than in a membrane.

title: Studying Ferroptosis in the Tumor Microenvironment.
takeaway: A commentary rather than new findings: it argues that ferroptosis should be treated as a microenvironmentally regulated process, attributing the failure of ferroptosis strategies to reach the clinic partly to the gap between conventional in vitro models and the real tumour microenvironment, and calls for multidisciplinary work linking foundational ferroptosis biology to clinically actionable interventions.
caveat: The abstract describes itself as a commentary that considers and calls for an approach, so it carries an argument rather than evidence of its own about ferroptosis.

title: Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis.
takeaway: Quantitative phosphoproteomics picks out mitochondrial fission factor (MFF) as a ferroptosis-selective regulator: the lipid mediator 17-HETE promotes MFF phosphorylation at Ser155, which fragments and disables both mitochondria and peroxisomes, intensifying interorganelle crosstalk and accelerating ferroptotic death. The authors built MFF-SPARK, a phase-separation biosensor, to track that phosphorylation in living cells, used it to identify PKC-beta and DUSP22 as a kinase-phosphatase pair governing it, and found avermectin B1 activates the PKC-beta-MFF axis.
caveat: The in vivo result the abstract reports is that avermectin B1 can sensitize tumours to ferroptosis; the mechanism, the biosensor and the kinase-phosphatase pair are cell-level, and the authors offer the work as a conceptual framework and toolbox.

title: LncRNA CCDC152 coordinates a tumor-associated selenoprotein P cycle that sustains selenium-dependent redox homeostasis in glioblastoma.
takeaway: Describes a tumour-adapted selenium recycling system in glioblastoma: cells secrete selenoprotein P, recapture it through LRP8 and reuse the selenium to keep selenoprotein levels and proliferation up, with the lncRNA CCDC152 coordinating it. Disrupting SELENOP or LRP8 suppressed proliferation, LRP8 depletion lowered GPX1 and GPX4, and CCDC152 depletion increased ferroptosis susceptibility — and unexpectedly CCDC152 raised SELENOP production in glioblastoma cells although it suppresses SELENOP translation in hepatocyte-derived cells.
caveat: Shown in glioblastoma cells, with the clinical part an association between SELENOP and CCDC152 expression and poor prognosis in IDH-mutant astrocytoma; the abstract says this selenium-utilization vulnerability "may be exploited" by ferroptosis-inducing therapies.

title: NRF2-mediated ferroptosis suppression defines a cancer-specific vulnerability in tumors.
takeaway: In an inducible Kras-driven mouse lung cancer model, deleting NRF2 on its own — with no drug given — eradicated cancer cells, reduced tumour burden and prolonged survival, while non-cancerous cells tolerated the same loss, as judged by single-cell RNA sequencing with AI-based genotype classification. The authors attribute the killing to ferroptosis induced inside established tumours without any exogenous inducer.
caveat: One Kras-driven mouse lung cancer model, and the ferroptosis attribution rests on the canonical ferroptotic gene and protein markers the abstract lists (Ptgs2, Acsl4, Tfrc; SO2/3-PRDX3, COX2, TfR1); NRF2 inhibition as a standalone therapy is where the authors position the finding, and the abstract is explicit that the experiment was genetic deletion rather than a pharmacologic agent.

title: Reprogramming of TLR-Ferroptosis Signaling and Immunometabolic Pathways Overcomes Myeloid Suppression to Improve Checkpoint Blockade in Prostate Cancer.
takeaway: Characterizes an ultrasmall PSMA-targeting silica particle therapy as a way to reprogram the TLR-ferroptosis axis in MYC-driven prostate cancer. As single agents the particles suppressed lipid and steroid biosynthesis, disrupted control of lipid peroxidation and impaired nutrient flux, sensitizing tumours to ferroptosis, while redox remodeling, stromal reprogramming and innate immune activation reversed myeloid suppression and brought in CD8+ T cells. Combined with CSF-1R inhibition and checkpoint blockade the particles suppressed tumour growth, extended survival beyond 100 days and reached up to 50% complete remission.
caveat: Those efficacy numbers come from MYC-overexpressing mouse models and from the three-way combination with CSF-1R inhibition and checkpoint blockade; where the abstract says "clinically validated" it is describing the particle platform, not this combination or its ferroptosis mechanism.

title: Safe lysosomal sequestration of ferrous iron is mediated via cholesterol shielding and drives senescence and ferroptosis resistance.
takeaway: Reports that senescent cells park ferrous iron in lysosomes and that this is needed for several senescence-associated phenotypes, and that two adaptations make the arrangement survivable: the Fe2+ load triggers lysosomal alkalinization and then cholesterol accumulation that reinforces the lysosomal membrane against permeabilization, while polyunsaturated fatty acids are partitioned into lipid droplets and so withdrawn from membranes. Together these give senescent cells robust ferroptosis resistance.
caveat: The abstract reports this in senescent cells without naming the model system, and puts the therapeutic angle as something that "may provide new opportunities" to target senescent cells rather than a result.

title: Intracellular complement factor H protects neurons during CNS inflammation.
takeaway: Identifies a non-canonical, intracellular job for complement factor H inside neurons. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of retinal ganglion cells from multiple sclerosis donors and controls found CFH expression strongly correlated with resilience to degeneration, and CFH was induced in retinal and other CNS neurons under inflammatory and oxidative stress, where it limited reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation from the endoplasmic reticulum. Protection required its C-terminal SCR20 domain and held without CFH secretion and without complement component C3.
caveat: The human evidence is a correlation between CFH expression and resilience in donor retinal ganglion cells, with mechanism worked out in mouse and human neurons; ferroptosis enters as the abstract describing the endoplasmic reticulum as a major site of lipid peroxidation during neuronal ferroptosis, and the implication for MS therapy is stated as an implication.
